articles.title: Denmark ratifies Trump deal over Greenland, hoping to end conflict
articles.summary: COPENHAGEN, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Denmark's parliament unanimously ratified a security agreement with the United States on Greenland on Thursday, hoping to end...
articles.body:
Vote on the security agreement between Denmark, Greenland, and the USA in the Parliament Hall, Copenhagen

COPENHAGEN, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Denmark's parliament unanimously ratified a security agreement with the United States on Greenland on Thursday, hoping to end a standoff over the Arctic island's future ‌that has rattled transatlantic relations.

The US, Denmark and Greenland signed the agreement in September after US President ‌Donald Trump repeatedly threatened to take control of the mineral-rich self-governing Danish territory of 57,000 people.

"This agreement modernizes the United States-Denmark-Greenland defence partnership and ​bolsters the national security of the United States and our allies in NATO," US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement posted on X.

The executive agreement takes effect once Denmark's foreign ministry tells the US in a diplomatic note that procedures are complete. It does not need approval from the US Senate.

It expands the US military's role in Greenland, including permission to ‌establish a "Golden Dome" missile defence system, while ⁠reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination.

The signatories will now start work on a new Greenland law to screen outside investors on security grounds and plans for two new ⁠US military bases, as outlined in the agreement, Denmark's Defence Minister Jeppe Bruus told Reuters.

"I expect that the US will now also start to be more concrete on the purposes and the arrangement around these two areas," he said.

Trump's refusal to rule out ​military or ​economic force to acquire the island triggered a diplomatic crisis ​within NATO in January and months of intensive ‌negotiations.

Naaja Nathanielsen, a Greenlandic member of the Danish parliament, said Trump's pressure had led to distrust in Greenland towards the US administration.

"It's been really difficult for Greenlanders these past two years. It's been seeping into every aspect of our lives," Nathanielsen told Reuters. She hoped the agreement would open a path to dialogue after hurtful rhetoric within the Western alliance.

Greenland's parliament ratified the deal this month. Danish lawmakers expressed relief and hope that the deal will normalize ‌the situation in Greenland.

Mikkel Vedby Rasmussen, a political science professor at ​the University of Copenhagen, said the deal was more likely a ​beginning than an end.

"With the treaty in hand, ​the US will be able to demand greater influence on decisions that have security policy implications ‌and on part of the extraction of strategic ​resources," he said.

Other experts say ​the new agreement does not add much US military access to Greenland. The northernmost US base is already in Greenland, which lies on the shortest route from Europe to North America.

Trump last month said that "massive oil, ​gas and mineral exploration" was set ‌to begin on Greenland, a contentious statement on a territory that has banned new drilling for crude. ​Denmark has said any resource extraction must respect local law.

(Reporting by Stine Jacobsen, editing by Jacob ​Gronholt-Pedersen, Louise Rasmussen, Rod Nickel, Thomas Derpinghaus and Chizu Nomiyama)

articles.title: Florida has approved protection for more than 50,000 acres of working ranches and farmland, including a 19,312-acre cattle property backed by a $77.75 million conservation easement near the Everglades
articles.summary: Florida's landscape is more than its beaches, bustling cities and sprawling neighbourhoods.
articles.body: Florida's landscape is more than its beaches, bustling cities and sprawling neighbourhoods. Beyond the familiar picture of the Sunshine State lies another Florida, one made up of cattle ranches, open grasslands, working farms, pine forests and wetlands that quietly sustain its agricultural economy and natural ecosystems. But as towns expand and development reshapes the landscape, these stretches of rural land face an increasingly important question: how can they continue to support agriculture without eventually being swallowed by urban growth?The answer, at least in part, lies in protecting the land without taking it away from the people who work on it. Instead of purchasing entire properties and turning them into government-owned conservation areas, Florida has been using conservation easements to permanently restrict future development while allowing existing farming, ranching and timber operations to continue. It is an approach that attempts to preserve both the state's agricultural livelihoods and the natural landscapes surrounding them.In its latest move, Florida has approved the protection of more than 50,000 acres of working agricultural land across six properties, including a 19,312-acre cattle and farming operation near the Everglades that will receive a $77.75 million conservation easement. According to the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS), the approvals were announced on November 17 through the state's Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, taking the total area protected under the initiative to more than 308,000 acres.A $77.75 million conservation easement for a 19,312-acre cattle propertyAmong the properties receiving protection is Osceola Prairie, an approximately 19,312-acre cattle and farming operation in Osceola County. The property will be protected through a $77.75 million conservation easement, which includes $15 million in funding from the US Department of Defense's Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration Programme.Located within the Kissimmee River Basin and the Northern Everglades ecosystem, the property includes pastures, wetlands, forests and natural prairie habitats. It also has seven centre-pivot irrigation systems used to grow field crops and hay for its cattle operation.The property is surrounded by several conservation areas, including Kissimmee Prairie Preserve State Park along its southern boundary. It is also located less than a mile from the Avon Park Air Force Range, making its protection relevant to the surrounding landscape and military installation.Six properties and more than 50,000 acres protectedThe approvals cover a range of agricultural and timber operations across Florida. These include the 10,208-acre Hill Grade Tract in Hendry County, which will receive a $46 million conservation easement. The land is primarily used for vegetable and row crop cultivation and helps connect existing protected areas, providing habitat support for the endangered Florida panther.Other projects include Spanish Trails Land and Farming, a 6,058-acre cattle ranch across Charlotte and DeSoto counties, and Pine Level Ranch, a 7,057-acre citrus and cattle operation across DeSoto and Hardee counties. Their conservation easements are valued at $33.3 million and $33.8 million, respectively.The remaining two properties are timber operations: the 4,668-acre Donaldson Tract in Alachua County and the 3,370-acre Loveridge property in Leon County. Both are being protected through conservation easements.All six properties are located within the Florida Wildlife Corridor and participate in the state's agricultural Best Management Practices programme.How conservation easements protect agricultural landUnder the Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, the state purchases development rights through conservation easements. This prevents the land from being converted for future development while allowing its owners to retain ownership and continue approved agricultural activities.The programme was established in 2001 to protect Florida's working agricultural lands as they face increasing pressure from development. The state legislature allocated $425 million to the programme in its 2026–27 budget, including funding specifically for larger conservation projects.According to FDACS, more than 243,000 acres have been permanently protected during Commissioner Wilton Simpson's administration. The latest approvals mark another milestone for the programme, which aims to preserve agricultural production while protecting natural resources and wildlife habitats.As Florida continues to grow, the challenge will be to make room for expanding communities without losing the agricultural landscapes that have long shaped the state. Protecting these properties through conservation easements offers a way to keep that balance, allowing ranches and farms to remain productive while safeguarding wetlands, wildlife habitats and open spaces from future development. The latest approvals are a reminder that conservation does not always mean leaving land untouched; sometimes, it means ensuring that the people who work the land can continue doing so for generations to come.You use AI every day. articles.title: Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say
articles.summary: European allies of Ukraine say they have a "united" negotiating position at a summit in Berlin.
articles.body:
European leaders have said they are ready for negotiations with Russia on ending the war in Ukraine, in a strong show of support for Kyiv.

"Europe has a clear and consistent and united negotiating position," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed that Moscow's "maximalist demands are not realistic".

They were speaking at Berlin's summit of Ukraine's allies known as the Coalition of the Willing.

US President Donald Trump's envoys were also there, and his son-in-law Jared Kushner said Trump wanted to make a deal with Russia "with Europe by his side". Russia's Vladimir Putin has so far rejected any European role in the US led peace talks.

Trump had earlier held historic trilateral talks in Shenzhen with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping and later dialled into the Berlin summit from Air Force One.

In a lengthy press conference following his talks with Trump and Xi, Putin addressed the question of multilateral peace talks, saying the Americans were "insistently" asking Russia to allow the Europeans to take part.

Putin claimed Russia was not against the idea but said Moscow wanted to clarify "what Europe will bring to these talks".

"That is why, through diplomatic channels, we have invited the Europeans to come to Moscow in order to determine their positions. And after that, we will decide in what format we will continue the dialogue with Ukraine."

But Putin also said that "every day" Russia heard that European leaders were talking about war coming in 2030. "But we are not planning to attack anyone... Is that normal? I do not think so," he said. Still, Putin added, Russia understood that "discussing issues linked to security in Europe is pointless without the Europeans".

Jared Kushner told reporters that the US president had come away from Shenzhen believing that "peace is achievable".

Striking an upbeat note, Kushner said that the Russians were willing to trust the instinct of the US envoys "on our behalf" that the Europeans should be at the table and that Moscow was now "comfortable" with Ukraine having security guarantees based on the idea enshrined in Nato's Article Five that requires allies to come to a country's defence if it comes under attack.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has long sought a guarantee equivalent to Nato's collective defence clause, and there has been little indication that Putin would accept that kind of condition. Russia has never accepted the idea of Ukrainian membership of Nato, but Article Five-style guarantees could theoretically be offered to Kyiv without being part of the Western defensive alliance.

Zelensky and the three European leaders - Merz, Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron - were not as upbeat as Kushner, and the Ukrainian president made clear that the Russian president had spurned every proposal so far: "Putin has always said no."

The German chancellor was equally sceptical, although he said with US involvement the chance of peace was increasing. Europe was willing to enter "serious discussions on European security" with Russia, he explained, "as long as it's matched with a serious discussion and only first a peace agreement with Ukraine".

"These talks have to begin, and we will accept if conditions are acceptable for Europe and Ukraine," said Merz.

There have been mixed messages from Moscow on European participation to the talks. Last week, following a visit to Moscow, Witkoff and Kushner appeared certain that Europe would soon have a seat at the negotiating table.

But the Russians were more circumspect and this week Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said a "great deal" would have to be done before the format could be expanded, suggesting that several more rounds of discussions would have to be held before any four-sided talks could take place.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

While Russia has engaged with several rounds of talks over the last year, little in Moscow's rhetoric or actions suggests that the Kremlin is considering scaling down its war on Ukraine.

It continues to pound Kyiv's energy infrastructure to cripple it as winter takes hold, increasing numbers of civilian casualties are being recorded across the country, and Kremlin officials haven't budged from Russia's demands for Ukraine sovereign territory.

As delegations were meeting in China and Germany on Thursday, several buildings in Kyiv's historic centre came under attack from drones. One person was killed in a strike on a residential building in the Podilskyi neighbourhood, while the Dutch and Austrian embassies as well as Saint Volodymyr's Cathedral reported damage.

And today, Putin vowed that Moscow's response to a Ukrainian strike on the Crimean Bridge linking Russia with occupied Crimea would be "considerably more painful" than what Kyiv had achieved.

He also said he had discussed a "possible ceasefire in a number of areas" but had decided against it after the attack on the bridge.

Still, Putin claimed to be "interested" in ending the war and was ready for making compromises, while Ukraine and Europe were not.

"I assure you, we have no desire at all to continue this armed conflict," Putin said.

articles.title: Children urge govt, politicians to prioritise kids for UP’s devpt
articles.summary: UP World Children’s Day: Unicef-led appeal in Lucknow urges govt, politicians to prioritise children in policies and budgets for development.
articles.body: Lucknow: On the eve of World Children’s Day, a children’s appeal titled ‘Bachche Aage Toh Uttar Pradesh Aage (When Children Move Forward, Uttar Pradesh Moves Forward)’ was released in Lucknow, to urge govt to draw up policies and budgets keeping in view the needs of children.Unicef and Centre for Child Rights at Dr Ram Manohar Lohiya National Law University organised the event under the theme ‘Children’s Future, Uttar Pradesh’s Future’. Children from villages and cities, including children with disabilities and those living in childcare institutions, took part.They spoke about artificial intelligence, environment and safety of children. Through drawings and stage performances, children shared what ‘My Day, My Rights, My Future’ meant to them.In a recorded video message, chairperson of the Uttar Pradesh Legislature’s Joint Committee on Women and Child Development, Anjula Mahaur, said children know whether their route to school is safe and whether they have a place to play.She said their experiences can help legislators and officials design better policies and programmes.Chief, Unicef Uttar Pradesh office, Dr Zakari Adam said: “If children are left behind, how can Uttar Pradesh move forward? We adults have a responsibility to listen carefully to their suggestions and take them into account when we make decisions.”Prof Amar Pal Singh, vice-chancellor of Dr Ram Manohar Lohiya National Law University, said, “Every child has potential. As adults, it is our responsibility to create an environment where children can understand their rights and develop their talents.”Nipurnh Gupta, communication specialist, Unicef Uttar Pradesh, said: “We asked children in villages and cities what they wanted to change in their daily lives. Their answers shaped this charter and the requests it puts before elected representatives.”Children also took part in a contest on anaemia prevention. articles.title: Stanlow refinery: Essar to pay £873k over wastewater breaches
articles.summary: Ten charges involved oil, cyanide and other pollutants entering local waterways.
articles.body:
One of the UK's largest oil refinery operators has been ordered to pay £873,473 after breaching environmental permit limits nearly 500 times over three years.

The Environment Agency (EA) said the Stanlow refinery in Ellesmere Port, Cheshire, exceeded wastewater discharge limits at least 489 times between 2018 and 2020. Essar Oil (UK) Limited pleaded guilty to 12 charges in March .

Essar Oil, which trades as EET Fuels, was fined £800,000 and ordered to pay £73,473 in costs at Warrington Magistrates' Court.

EET Fuels said it regretted the "historic incidents" and had invested more than £24m to improve environmental performance.

Ten charges related to wastewater discharges containing oil, suspended solids and chemicals, including cyanide, into Thornton Brook, the River Gowy and the Manchester Ship Canal.

Two other charges concerned incidents in 2019.

In February 2019, between 15 and 20 tonnes of a chemical leaked into the ship canal after a vent was left open and a written procedure was not followed.

A month later, a contractor's vehicle ruptured an effluent pipe. During repairs, about 15 tonnes of partially treated sewage entered Thornton Brook, which leads to the protected Mersey Estuary.

Environment Agency officers reported a sheen of oil on local waterways, while vegetation downstream of the refinery's discharge point was blackened by oil in January 2020.

The company was fined £80,000 for each of the 10 offences, with no additional penalty for the two 2019 incidents. Three breaches from 2022 and 2023 were taken into consideration without further punishment.

Nigel Glasgow, the Environment Agency's area environment manager, said the case showed "a repeated failure to comply" with permit conditions.

An EET Fuels spokesperson said: "We take our environmental responsibilities extremely seriously and regret these historic incidents."

The company said its investment included rerouting wastewater to United Utilities' Ellesmere Port treatment works, resulting in "a significant improvement in environmental performance", including fewer discharges and reduced freshwater use.

articles.title: I started my career from minus Rs 1 crore: IIT-Delhi graduate recounts how family debt pushed him to strive but he never gave up on his dream. Left Google to start his own app that now has Silicon Valley's backing
articles.summary: An IIT Delhi graduate who discovered that his family was buried under more than ₹1 crore in debt during his second year of college has shared how he went
articles.body: An IIT Delhi graduate who discovered that his family was buried under more than ₹1 crore in debt during his second year of college has shared how he went from taking an ₹18 lakh-a-year job to working at Google, building a ₹2 crore mobile gaming business and eventually securing $400,000 in funding for his own AI startup.Yash Garg, a former Google employee and founder of a startup backed by Silicon Valley venture capital firm South Park Commons, narrated his journey in a lengthy LinkedIn post, describing how his family's financial crisis forced him to put his entrepreneurial ambitions on hold. “Most people start their careers with some privilege, and many start from zero. I started from minus ₹1 crore, and I did not even know it until my second year at IIT Delhi,” Garg wrote.His family's financial troubles stemmed from his father's real estate investments in under-construction flats by developers including Jaypee and Wave. His father had paid most of the property prices upfront using home loans, but the flats were never delivered on time. The banks, however, continued demanding monthly instalments. His parents initially borrowed money from friends and relatives before turning to credit cards to manage the repayments. They kept the extent of the debt hidden from their children.The situation became impossible to conceal when collection agents started visiting their home and demanding payments. Garg said he could see the stress taking a toll on his mother.He said he sat his parents down and asked them to list every person and institution they owed money to. As he wrote down the amounts owed to banks, relatives, friends and credit card companies, the principal alone crossed ₹1 crore. “That day, I knew I had to grow up quickly and get my parents out of this situation,” he recalled.Rejected by Tower Research, settles for ₹18 lakh jobGarg had joined IIT Delhi with plans of starting his own company after graduation. But the debt forced him to change course. He decided to secure a high-paying job and clear his family's loans within two years before returning to his entrepreneurial ambitions. He set his sights on high-frequency trading (HFT) firms, which offered annual packages of more than ₹50 lakh. With a 9.7/10 CGPA and the second-highest rank in his department, he believed he had a strong chance.But his placement plans suffered a major setback on the first day of campus recruitment. He prioritized Tower Research, cleared three interview rounds but was rejected in the final round. The disappointment affected his performance in other interviews, and by the end of the day, the companies that had shortlisted him had moved on. The following day, he accepted an offer from Cohesity worth ₹18 lakh annually, he said, giving a detailed account of his placement journey.He moved to Bengaluru in July 2019, lived in a paying guest accommodation and kept his monthly expenses below ₹20,000. He ate meals at the office, avoided social outings and sent almost everything he earned back home.Next stop: US, UKRealizing that his salary would not be enough to clear the debt quickly, he began preparing for opportunities in the US. He taught himself competitive programming and eventually achieved Master rank on Codeforces.In January 2020, he started applying to Google and other companies in the US and UK. The pandemic disrupted international recruitment just weeks later.Around the same time, Garg joined travel technology startup Spotnana as a founding engineer. He hoped the startup's growth and his equity would eventually help him earn enough to repay his family's loans.But after a year of sending money home, he discovered that almost his entire salary had gone towards interest payments on credit card debt. The principal remained untouched, and the list of outstanding loans was exactly as long as before.He described it as one of the lowest points of his life.Despite working weekdays and weekends and being among the company's top performers, his appraisal raise was not enough to make a meaningful difference. He also tried launching a programming YouTube channel and learning Android development to generate additional income, but neither effort brought in money.A conversation with a college senior who worked at Google eventually changed his direction. The senior told him that remaining at Spotnana could mean taking more than four years to clear the debt, rather than the two years he had originally planned.Google happened to GargAfter four months of intensive preparation, during which he also faced rejections from Uber and Coinbase, Google offered him a position on its Search team. Garg described receiving the selection call as one of the happiest moments of his life, saying he finally saw a realistic path towards freeing his parents from debt.When Garg joined Google, approximately ₹80 lakh of the family debt remained. His salary alone would take years to clear it.Working 100 hours a week for gaming businessHe decided to start a mobile applications business with his father, with Google's permission, working nights and weekends.Initially, the duo developed Android applications and games but failed to generate revenue. Garg then studied the differences between the Android and iOS markets and decided to shift their focus to Apple's ecosystem.He spent ₹2.1 lakh on a MacBook Pro, selected their most downloaded Android game, rebuilt it in Apple's Swift programming language in six days and launched it on iOS.The gamble paid off almost immediately. The game attracted strong downloads, and within days of enabling monetization, its earnings had covered the cost of the laptop.Revenue increased from ₹6 lakh in the first month to ₹24 lakh by the fourth month as they added more games.Garg said he was working close to 100 hours a week between his Google job and the gaming business. Over 18 months, their games accumulated more than 200,000 downloads, primarily from users in the US, and generated over ₹2 crore in revenue.Together with his Google salary, the earnings allowed the family to start repaying the actual loan principal rather than merely servicing interest.In June 2023, they finally cleared the last outstanding loan.“The list I had written in my second year of college was finally empty. My parents were free, and after years of waiting, so was I,” he wrote.Garg resigned from Google immediately after the debt was paid off. His last working day was the day before his 25th birthday, he recalledWith savings from the gaming business, Garg finally had the freedom to pursue entrepreneurship full-time. However, his first attempt did not go as planned. He developed 12 new games over four months, but none succeeded. Changes to Apple's iOS privacy policies had disrupted the economics of hyper-casual gaming, forcing him to reconsider his business model. He shut down the games business and pivoted to software-as-a-service (SaaS), initially exploring applications for Shopify.After realizing the competition was too intense and he lacked a differentiated idea, he studied around 70 B2B SaaS marketplaces to identify another opportunity.He eventually chose monday.com, a project management platform, and started Super Workday, developing applications for teams using the service. His first application failed because it targeted too narrow a market. For the next product, he studied customer feature requests and identified the platform's biggest unresolved problem. The approach worked. In April 2024, after eight months without generating any revenue since leaving Google, he secured his first paying customer.He began launching a new application every month.According to his LinkedIn post, Super Workday now operates largely on autopilot, has more than 300 paying customers, mostly in the US, and is approaching $100,000 in annual recurring revenue (ARR).The business also helped him pay for his sister's wedding, something he described as a particularly proud moment.South Park Commons invests $400,000 in AI startupWith the SaaS business generating stable income, Garg finally felt ready to pursue a venture-scale idea.He began developing an AI executive assistant and, in January 2025, secured $400,000 in funding from South Park Commons at a valuation of $5.7 million.Garg said receiving the investment made the years of waiting and setbacks feel worthwhile.“My startup journey is still early. Since then, there have been many more ups and downs, and there are still many things to figure out,” he wrote. “But for the first time, I am building the startup I always wanted to build, and I am ready for whatever comes next.”You use AI every day.
